function.name: user_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a user based on the provided user name and the status of the mandates. This API is intended for use by partners to retrieve information about their clients' mandates. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

name.description: The full name of the partner's client for whom to fetch mandates.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If omitted, mandates of all statuses will be retrieved.

function.name: partner_mandates
function.description: Fetches the mandates associated with a partner based on the specified status. If no status is provided, all mandates are retrieved. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

status.description: The status of the mandates to be fetched. If left empty, mandates with any status will be retrieved.

message.content:
A **mandate** is a formal instruction or authorization that a client gives to a service provider (often a bank, payment platform, or financial institution) to act on their behalf. Think of it as a “give‑me‑permission” document that tells the provider what they’re allowed to do, for how long, and under what conditions. ### Key points | Aspect | What it means | |--------|---------------| | **Purpose** | Gives the provider the legal right to perform specific actions (e.g., debit a bank account, make payments, manage investments). | | **Typical use cases** | • Direct debit mandates for recurring bill payments
• Standing orders for scheduled transfers
• Investment mandates for portfolio management | | **Lifecycle** | • **Pending** – created but not yet activated (e.g., awaiting client signature or bank confirmation).
• **Active** – fully approved and operational.
• **Inactive** – cancelled, expired, or revoked. | | **Legal standing** | Usually governed by local regulations (e.g., PSD2 in the EU, NACHA rules in the US). | ### In the context of the API you’re working with The API exposes two helper functions: 1. **`user_mandates`** – fetches mandates for a specific client (by name) and optionally filters by status (`active`, `pending`, `inactive`). 2. **`partner_mandates`** – fetches all mandates belonging to the partner (your organization) and can also filter by status. These functions let partners retrieve the mandates that have been issued to their clients, so they can monitor, audit, or manage them programmatically. --- #### Quick example ```python # Get all active mandates for a client named "Acme Corp" mandates = user_mandates(name="Acme Corp", status="active") ``` This call would return a list of mandate objects that are currently active for Acme Corp. --- **Bottom line:** A mandate is a formal, legally binding instruction that authorizes a third party to act on your behalf, and the API lets you pull those records for reporting or operational purposes.
